fichas.title: Group room
fichas.summary: The group room is the main space used by children in a daycare centre. It should offer varied activity zones, potentially including a second level and a play stage with a snug cave. It should be close to the WC area, ideally have direct outdoor access, and face south.

fichas.title: Outdoor areas and pond
fichas.summary: Daycare outdoor areas should offer varied play and landscape experiences. Suggested features include hills, planting, gardens, sandpits, bird tables, dry stone walls, meadows, and a pond. The pond guidance specifies a minimum water surface, depth, and safety measures.
furniture_equipment: Coarse net or builder's steel mesh

dimensions.label: Pond depth
dimensions.context: Recommended pond depth; the text says this is to avoid oxygen deficiency.
dimensions.ocr_raw:
CHILDREN'S DAYCARE
Rooms, Outdoor Areas

Group room
Most time in the children's daycare centre is spent here. Required
floor area approx. 2.5 m2 per child. Create zones as varied as
possible and design a second floor level and a stage (play-stage
half-open, with a snug cave). Play decks up to a height of 1.50 m
must have a handrail at least 70 em high; play decks more than
1.50 m high must have handrails min. 1.00 m high. The group
room should have as short a distance as possible to the WC
area. Ideally, provide direct access to the open air and align to
the south.

Outdoor areas
Outside playgrounds should be designed to be as varied as possible. The design of external works for children's centres is regulated by several standards. The stipulated minimum area outside
per child is variable between the German states.

Rest or sleeping rooms
These are not always considered necessary, as mattresses are often laid out in the group room for the midday sleep (cupboard to
store the mattresses -7 p. 188 0).

Compost heap as the core of an organic garden. Semi-shaded
location for organic waste from the centre.

Kitchen
The status of the kitchen in the children's centre can vary according to the paedagogical concept, for example a central kitchen for
all groups or as a series of kitchens, one in each group room. Different floor heights are recommended so that adults and children
can cook together.

Hilly landscape Modelling the terrain by heaping and excavating
the ground surface. The coarse shape is produced by a hydraulic
excavator, and the fine modelling by hand. The hills can incorporate plants, shrubs, hedges, flowers and clover of various heights.

Trees for climbing, to provide shade, deliver fruit and be educational. Also worth considering are vegetable/herb gardens,
sandpits, bird tables, dry stone walls, meadows etc.
Pond should have min. 6 m2 water surface and a depth of 80 em
to avoid oxygen deficiency. For safety reasons, either a coarse net
should be spread over the water or builder's steel mesh installed
10 em under the water surface.

fichas.title: Rest, kitchen, and dining spaces
fichas.summary: Rest rooms are optional where mattresses can be laid out in the group room for midday sleep. Kitchen arrangements may be centralized or distributed among group rooms; different floor heights are recommended to support adults and children cooking together. The group room is normally used for meals, although an extended corridor or entrance hall may also serve as a communal eating place.
